title: We are staying: European diplomats reject Russian calls to leave Ukraine
gist: More than twenty EU embassies publicly refused the Kremlin's October 3 call for diplomats to leave Kyiv, framing it as intimidation. Peter Dickinson argues Russia's strategy has shifted to breaking Ukrainian civilian morale via winter infrastructure strikes and cutting off European support through hybrid warfare, while Europe has yet to impose tangible costs on Moscow.

themes.theme: Kremlin pressure on Kyiv diplomatic corps

insights.claim: Russia issued a statement on October 3, 2026 urging foreign diplomatic missions to immediately leave Ukraine, repeating a similar appeal made in May amid an escalation of strikes on Kyiv.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Repeated evacuation demands signal Moscow intends further escalation against the Ukrainian capital.

insights.claim: More than twenty EU embassies responded to Russia's call to leave Kyiv by publicly declaring "We are staying," and the EU ambassador said all 25 member states with embassies in Kyiv would remain.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Visible European diplomatic commitment suggests no near-term collapse in EU political backing for Ukraine.

insights.claim: EU Ambassador to Ukraine Katarina Mathernova interprets Russia's repeated threats to diplomats as a sign of Kremlin frustration at failing to gain the upper hand on the battlefield.

insights.claim: The author judges that European refusal to evacuate embassies from Kyiv, while a morale boost for Ukrainians, is unlikely to deter the Kremlin on its own.
